steps.what: Select threat intelligence evidence and presentation messages
Write threat intelligence slide text and speaker notes

loop.purpose: Draft slide wording from selected messages and evidence
loop.input: checked presentation brief with audience and source references
loop.output: slide outline with titles, bullets, notes and source references
loop.check: Compare every claim and implication with the evidence; preserve dates, uncertainty and audience meaning
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; tester writes unsupported or unclear sections manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Clear threat explanations vary with the audience and cannot be reduced to fixed mail-merge text

steps.what: Lay out presentation slides using the checked outline
Verify presentation claims, readability and final distribution version

tasks.design: The tester selects evidence and messages in {DOCS}, then checks a bounded draft of slide text and notes. Native presentation templates lay out that outline, and the tester verifies the exact final deck before sharing it internally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Presentation production repeats wording and layout work after the intelligence judgement is complete.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting and native outline-to-slide layouts can reduce composition and formatting effort.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining uncertain threat information without implying unsupported urgency or local exposure.
tasks.human_edge: The tester chooses the message, checks evidence and anticipates how the audience will interpret it.
tasks.altitude: Less routine slide assembly; intelligence selection and audience judgement stay with the tester.

reach.task: Brief system owners on relevant threat evidence

evidence.claim: Constrained slide drafting and native template assembly are plausible; the proposed presentation time reduction is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is presentation development after intelligence gathering, excluding initial intelligence collection and live delivery. Those tasks must not claim the same preparation gain.
The tester produces the checked brief in s1: audience, chosen messages, source references, dates, uncertainty and permitted disclosure. All evidence selection and capture time remains counted.

The drafting step proposes slide number, title, bullets, speaker notes and source references. The tester checks and corrects these exact fields in s2, whose remaining time includes capture and editing. Only the checked outline feeds s3; missing or incompatible fields are assembled manually and count against savings.
Test native templates and outline import before custom generation. Existing automatic layout runtime earns no new labour saving.
research_questions: Do source checks and layout repairs leave a net reduction in total presentation preparation time?

already_counted.description: Evidence selection and final presentation verification
Meaning checks and structured outline corrections

incremental.description: Maintain the layout mapping and inspect drafting examples

approvals.approved_version: Exact final slide and notes version, evidence references, disclosure scope and internal recipients; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R73 gives gross27 and net20 after7 upkeep. Range3-12% assumes repeated manual assembly of short source-linked briefings and allows detailed editing and layout repairs; no intelligence judgement or live delivery saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Less slide composition and layout, with evidence and audience decisions retained.
reach: Prepare evidence-based threat briefings for system owners
role.ambitious_version: A tester who explains credible threats clearly enough for operational owners to act.
